sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the advantage of ten is in all matters of Torah and mitzvos, but its primary advantage is in prayer, and the superiority of communal prayer over individual prayer is essential to the prayer itself, and likewise the advantage of Torah study by ten is an essential matter.

translations.translation: Now, it is explained in Tanya
that the advantage of ten is in all matters of Torah and mitzvos,
for there is nothing holy in less than ten.
Nevertheless,
the primary advantage of ten is in prayer.
For the advantage of communal prayer is that it is desirable and accepted always,
and since the request of prayer is that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfill his request,
the advantage of communal prayer over individual prayer is not that in communal prayer an additional matter is added,
but rather,
this pertains to the prayer itself.
Based on this, it can be said,
that what is stated in the maamar, that the advantage in Torah of many is analogous to the advantage of communal prayer,
the intention in this is
(also)
that the advantage in Torah of many is in an essential matter.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that while the advantage of Torah study by ten could be understood as perfecting the acquisition of Torah, this explanation is insufficient because the parallel to communal prayer is in the drawing down of a higher light.

translations.translation: At first glance, one could explain this,
that since Torah is only acquired in a group,
it is understood,
that when Torah study is in a larger group,
the Torah is acquired more.
And since the perfection of a group is in ten,
for ten Jews are an example of and include all ten types of Israel,
as mentioned above,
therefore,
when Torah study is in ten,
the acquisition of Torah is in perfection.
But this explanation is insufficient.
For the aforementioned advantage in Torah of many is in the person engaged in Torah,
that when he studies in ten,
his acquisition
(that he acquires the Torah and receives it)
is in perfection.
And the parallel of Torah by many to communal prayer is in the drawing down.
As is explicit in the maamar,
that just as the many in their prayer draw down the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, so too, through Torah by many, a higher light is drawn down.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Thirteen Rules by which the Torah is expounded correspond to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, and through Torah study by many, specifically, these Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are drawn down.

translations.translation: And in order to explain the advantage of the drawing down through Torah of many,
the maamar prefaces,
that Rabbi Yishmael says
that the Torah is expounded by thirteen rules, through a kal vachomer and a gezeirah shavah, etc.
And he explains,
that through each and every rule
(of the thirteen rules by which the Torah is expounded)
new matters are revealed.
And the reason for this is,
that the thirteen rules by which the Torah is expounded correspond to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
And according to the teaching of the Maggid,
that when Moshe said, "El, please heal her please,"
where the name El is the first attribute
of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy,
the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him a kal vachomer,
"And if her father had but spit in her face, etc., a kal vachomer for the Shechinah,"
the first rule of the thirteen rules by which the Torah is expounded.
And the maamar adds,
that this is also the connection of the two interpretations of "He who pastures among roses,"
"Do not read shoshanim (roses) but sheshonim (who review) in the laws,"
and "Just as a rose has thirteen leaves, so too the Congregation of Israel has thirteen attributes of mercy,"
and the connection of the two interpretations is
that through the study of Torah
(that they review in the laws)
the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are drawn down.
And this is that through Torah of many a higher light is drawn down,
for this, that through Torah study the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are drawn down, is
primarily specifically through Torah study by many.
